@graph.name: C-CDA R2.1 XML
@graph.description: The Cascade Bridge Adapter for C-CDA R2.1 XML: the package of data a Cascade Bridge runs to turn a C-CDA ClinicalDocument, as a patient portal hands one out, into Cascade records. Import-only. This crate is the adapter's manifest: a Bridge reads the root entity first, for the format id, the source media type, the source schema, the envelope, the detect rule, the document table query, the mappings and the findings queries, the concept maps, the profile the Bridge must offer, the vocabulary repository and the paths, in it, of the ontology and shapes files the adapter is read against, the gap scheme every finding takes its body from, each gap declaring the sh:resultSeverity its findings carry where that is not sh:Info, the source accounting, and the test manifest. The data entities carry provenance for every committed file, and a sha256 computed locally over the committed bytes of each digested one. Seven inputs are copied byte for byte from the conformance repository's fixtures/ccda at the commit isBasedOn names; the others are authored here, and each says so.

@graph.description: A C-CDA as a portal hands it out: the ClinicalDocument is the document element and the one source record, and the mappings make a record of each clinical statement in it; docs/format.md, "The envelope".

@graph.name: Detect rule
@graph.description: An ASK over the envelope skeleton: true where the ClinicalDocument has a templateId child whose root is the US Realm Header's, 2.16.840.1.113883.10.20.22.1.1.

@graph.name: Document table: the clinical statements
@graph.description: One row per clinical statement this release maps: its slots, its class, its selector refined from the document element, its identifier, and the fingerprints of its key and of its members, with each class's key fields and member exclusions declared.

@graph.name: Mapping: records, versions and arrivals
@graph.description: For each row of the document table: the record, named by the Cascade Bridge Specification's rows for a C-CDA record from its class, identifier, key fingerprint or members fingerprint; its class, its source URL where its identifier names it, and its source id; its version, the patient the version is about, and the version's arrival with its selector.

@graph.name: Mapping: patient
@graph.description: A patientRole's first given and family name and its birth date.

@graph.name: Mapping: allergy
@graph.description: An Allergy Intolerance Observation's allergen, allergen codes, type, category, status, criticality, severity, reaction, manifestation codes and onset.

@graph.name: Mapping: the document's author
@graph.description: The custodian organisation's name, as the document's prov:qualifiedAttribution in the role rec:author.

@graph.name: Findings: sections not mapped
@graph.description: Each section whose templateIds name none this release maps, valued by its code.

@graph.name: Findings: entries not mapped
@graph.description: Each entry of a mapped section from which no record is made, valued by the least templateId root its statement claims.

@graph.name: Findings: allergy codes not mapped

@graph.name: Findings: problem codes not mapped

@graph.name: Findings: immunization and procedure codes not mapped

@graph.name: Mapping: medication

@graph.name: Findings: records named by their class alone

@graph.name: C-CDA R2.1 XML gaps
@graph.description: The scheme every finding this adapter reports takes its body from: one skos:Concept per gap, in this adapter's own namespace (https://ns.cascadeprotocol.org/adapter/ccda/v1-draft#), each under one of the bridge:gapKinds the Cascade Bridge Specification declares.

@graph.name: View comparison with cascade-cli
@graph.description: The views over the Bridge's graph for every input agree on every field they select with the same fields of cascade-cli's convert --from c-cda --to turtle for that input, read through the corrections in hasPart; an allergy's severity and a procedure's CPT code, which no view selects, were compared directly, through the same corrections; record names and provenance are not compared. Run once on 2026-10-07, outside CI, and for the medication and lab result views on 2026-10-07 over the inputs holding a medication or a result (epic-summarization, full-summarization, labs-section, medications-and-results-a, -b and -edges), with cascade-bridge-rs at the merge of its step 3 and cascade-cli at the commit isBasedOn names.

@graph.name: Never written
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes no patient source id, no allergen code, no allergy status, verification, criticality or onset, and no immunization or procedure status, no medication intent, status or end date, and no result status or interpretation, so those fields are not compared.

@graph.name: Concern act id
@graph.description: cascade-cli takes an allergy's source id from its concern act, and from the observation only where the act has none; the adapter's record is the observation, as the specification's C-CDA naming says, so an allergy's source id is not compared.

@graph.name: Names not read through originalText
@graph.description: cascade-cli names an allergen, a problem, a vaccine, a procedure, a drug and a test by the playing entity's name or the code's displayName, and never through the narrative an originalText references or the originalText's own text; the adapter reads those first. The names differ only where an input states such a reference or text (custodian-and-author, download-c, download-d, procedures, medications-and-results-a and -b), and are compared nowhere.

@graph.name: Negation ignored
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes a problem whose negationInd is true as active; the adapter writes it refuted, with no status. A negated problem's status and verification status are not compared.

@graph.name: Procedure acts
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes a Procedure Activity Act as a procedure; the adapter reports it as ccda:entryNotMapped. That record (procedures, PACT-31) is not compared.

@graph.name: Predicate renames
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes cascade:givenName, cascade:familyName, cascade:sourceRecordId, for a procedure health:performedDate, for a medication health:startDate and health:endDate, and for a result health:referenceRangeText, where the adapter writes foaf:givenName, foaf:familyName, the kind's sourceRecordId, clinical:procedureDate, clinical:startDate, clinical:endDate and health:referenceRange.

@graph.name: Severity on a reaction
@graph.description: cascade-cli reads an allergy's severity only from a Severity Observation on the allergy itself, never from its reaction, where C-CDA R2.1 puts it; the adapter reads both (custodian-and-author).

@graph.name: CPT in a translation
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes no CPT code a procedure states in a translation; the adapter writes clinical:cptCode from it (procedures).

@graph.name: Codes as IRIs
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes a CVX code as an IRI in http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/cvx/ (health:cvxCode) and a procedure's SNOMED CT code as an IRI (health:snomedCode), each read as the code alone; a SNOMED CT IRI in http://snomed.info/id/ is read as in http://snomed.info/sct/.

@graph.name: Dose as dosage
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes a medication's doseQuantity value as clinical:dosage; the adapter writes a Medication Free Text Sig's text and reports a structured dose as ccda:structuredDosage, so a dosage is not compared.

@graph.name: Codes in a translation
@graph.description: cascade-cli reads an RxNorm or a LOINC code only from a drug's or a test's own code, never from a translation; the adapter reads both (medications-and-results-a and -b). The code is compared where cascade-cli states one.

@graph.name: LOINC IRI space
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes a test code as http://loinc.org/ and the code, where the adapter writes http://loinc.org/rdf/ and the code; each is read as the code alone.

@graph.name: Times narrowed
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes a medication's start as a date, its time of day left off; the adapter's date-time is read as its day.

@graph.name: Range and coded value unread
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes a reference range only from its own text, as [object Object] where the text is a narrative reference, and never from an IVL_PQ, and writes no value of a coded result; each is compared where cascade-cli states it, the placeholder read as absent (medications-and-results-a and -b).

@graph.name: Vital signs as records
@graph.description: cascade-cli makes a record of a Vital Sign Observation inside a Result Organizer; the adapter makes none, and reports it as ccda:resultComponentNotMapped. That record (medications-and-results-a and -b, VS-9103) is not compared.

@graph.name: Two values unread
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes no value and no unit of a result stating two values; the adapter carries the first and reports the second as ccda:onlyFirstCarried (medications-and-results-edges, LAB-9503). The value and unit are compared where cascade-cli states them.
